claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A multi-scale, multi-fidelity machine-learning surrogate can simultaneously predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
The surrogate can use a limited number of first-principles, CALPHAD, and targeted experimental data points.
Multi-scale descriptors can encode the material’s hierarchical heterogeneity and chemical-fluctuation profiles.
The hierarchical microstructure and chemical-fluctuation profiles mediate correlations between local descriptors and macroscopic mechanical properties.
Microstructural descriptors enable the surrogate to capture nonlinear correlations between the hierarchical heterostructure and mechanical response.
The surrogate can bypass computationally intensive atomistic or phase-diagram simulations.
The proposed approach will reduce computational cost relative to conventional first-principles and CALPHAD approaches.
The proposed approach is expected to achieve a 5–10-fold computational speed-up over traditional methods.
The proposed approach is expected to improve predictive accuracy by 20–30% against targeted experimental benchmarks.
The intended applicability domain is ambient-temperature tensile and fracture testing while the microstructure remains intact.
Significant phase transformations or chemical segregation outside the ranges represented by the descriptors would reduce model reliability.
Descriptors that fail to capture unforeseen chemical or phase fluctuations would reduce model reliability.
Training data that do not span the full range of heterogeneity would reduce model reliability.
Predictions may not remain reliable for substantially different loading conditions, including multiaxial stress states.
The model is to be falsified if mean prediction deviation exceeds 30% or measured speed-up is less than five-fold relative to conventional methods.
